language_instruction: **Source language:** Classical (literary) Mongolian in the traditional Uighur-Mongol vertical script, printed from woodblocks (Beijing Kanjur, 1718–20). It is NOT Manchu. Columns run top to bottom and are read from LEFT to RIGHT. Transcribe in Mongolian script (Unicode U+1800 block), one source column per line, in reading order. The margin carries a Chinese section/volume/folio label. Report the primary language in the <language> tag.

translation.text:
<meta>Pothi-format woodblock leaf printed in red ink, from the Mongolian Kanjur of 1718–1720. Volume 7, folio 2. The body text was not transcribed because the scan resolution is too low, so this page has no running text to translate. The Chinese margin label is the only readable text.</meta>
<warning>The image is rotated 90° and the faded red Uighur-Mongol script cannot be read at this resolution. The body text and the Mongolian margin label were not transcribed, so they appear below only as <unclear> placeholders. A higher-resolution scan, or crops of individual columns, is needed before this page can be translated.</warning>

<note>Header: "Sūtras of Various Classes, volume seven, upper, two" <note>original: "諸品經第七卷上二"</note></note>

<note>A double rectangular frame with a continuous scrolling floral border surrounds the text block. Small framed panels on the left and right hold the margin labels, and the corners carry ornaments. This decorated frame is typical of the imperial Kangxi-era woodblock printing of the Mongolian Kanjur.</note>

<margin><unclear>Mongolian margin label, about 4 words (volume and folio indication), not transcribed</unclear></margin>

<unclear>about 17 columns of Classical Mongolian text in Uighur-Mongol script, printed in red ink, not transcribed: illegible at this resolution</unclear>

<margin><term>Zhupin jing</term> <gloss>Sūtras of Various Classes</gloss>, volume seven, upper, folio two <note>original: "諸品經第七卷上二". The Chinese label was used by the printers and binders of the Beijing edition to keep the loose leaves in order. "Sūtras of Various Classes" names a section of the Kanjur, the Buddhist canon of scriptures held to be the Buddha's own words. "上" ("upper") most likely marks the first part of the volume or one side of the leaf.</note></margin>

<summary>This is folio 2 of volume 7 in the "Sūtras of Various Classes" section of the red-ink Mongolian Kanjur printed in Beijing in 1718–1720. The Mongolian scripture text on the leaf could not be read from the available image, so only the Chinese margin label is translated.</summary>
<keywords>Mongolian Kanjur, Kangxi edition, 1718–1720, Sūtras of Various Classes, Zhupin jing, Buddhist canon, red-ink woodblock print, pothi format, Uighur-Mongol script, Chinese margin label, untranscribed page</keywords>
